sources.title: PowerSync Handling Update Conflicts
sources.released_version_or_commit: Repository main branch; exact commit SHA not captured (UNKNOWN).
sources.locator: Source file rendered lines 192–212; ordered client upload queue, backend-defined handling, simplest per-field LWW, idempotency, per-client incrementing operation ID, example validation.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official PowerSync documentation source and searched/read the rendered conflict-handling passage.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Backend behavior is app-defined; the simplest implementation uses per-field LWW; queued operations can be repeated; per-client operation IDs may support deduplication; custom validation/conflict handling is possible.
sources.applicability: Supports an explicit backend contract and idempotency proposal; does not provide cross-client ordering, claim fairness, or authorization policy.

sources.title: Apache CouchDB replication and conflict model
sources.released_version_or_commit: CouchDB documentation 3.5 stable branch; exact patch version not pinned.
sources.locator: Sections 2.3.1–2.3.3: replicated branches/default winner, single-node stale-revision 409, revision-tree leaves and application conflict resolution.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official CouchDB 3.5 conflict guide and inspected replication, conflict-winner and revision-tree passages.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Replication retains branches; default reads/views show a deterministic winner; a stale _rev update on one node is rejected with 409; merging branches is application-specific.
sources.applicability: Validates the draft's warning about hidden branches and its requirement for application-level business reconciliation.

sources.title: Apache CouchDB database security API
sources.released_version_or_commit: CouchDB documentation 3.5 stable branch; exact patch version not pinned.
sources.locator: GET/PUT /{db}/_security; members/admins, membership behavior and permissions.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official API reference and reviewed the database-security model.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Database membership grants database-wide access according to the documented member/admin roles; it does not itself define the app's volunteer-specific row/field authorization model.
sources.applicability: Supports the draft's caveat that group membership is not a complete fine-grained volunteer policy.

sources.title: Automerge document conflict reference
sources.released_version_or_commit: Current documentation; copyright 2026; exact library release/commit not displayed (UNKNOWN).
sources.locator: Conflicts section, especially same-property winner and getConflicts behavior; lines 60–112 in rendered source.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official reference at the conflict section and read the same-property, conflict API and operation-ordering passages.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Concurrent same-property updates yield a deterministic winner with alternatives queryable via getConflicts; a subsequent assignment resolves/removes the conflict record; ordering uses operation counter then actor ID, not wall-clock time.
sources.applicability: Supports using Automerge for collaborative content only with app-level state rules and a separate durable event log if history is required.

sources.title: PostgreSQL 18 INSERT documentation
sources.released_version_or_commit: PostgreSQL 18 current documentation; no Git commit applicable.
sources.locator: INSERT / ON CONFLICT arbiter and atomic insert-or-update behavior.
sources.observed_operation: Opened PostgreSQL's official current INSERT reference and inspected ON CONFLICT and atomicity passages.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A unique constraint/index can arbitrate ON CONFLICT; DO UPDATE has an atomic insert-or-update result under concurrency when the arbiter and statement conditions are satisfied; partial uniqueness must match the intended schema/predicate.
sources.applicability: Supports a canonical active-claim invariant in the proposed relational service, not offline arbitration fairness or business policy.

sources.title: MDN Storage quotas and eviction criteria
sources.released_version_or_commit: Current MDN article, last modified 2026-01-05 at access; no release/commit applicable.
sources.locator: Sections on QuotaExceededError, best-effort versus persistent storage, eviction under pressure and origin-wide eviction.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the MDN reference and read the quota, eviction and persistence passages.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Writes can exceed quota; best-effort origin data can be evicted under browser/device policies; persistence status and quotas differ by browser; eviction can remove all data for an origin.
sources.applicability: Supports bounded cache, explicit storage errors, and platform-specific durability validation; it does not promise draft survival after eviction.
